_comment: An ice_mage-kitted PC fixture for the [Ice Floor] area-terrain proof (ice_floor_loop). Mirrors near_mage_cast's shape/route (floodplains, met_relc banked so Relc's 'meet' node offers the Spar option directly) but classes {ice_mage:10} instead of {mage:1} -- VERIFIED via progression.gd's inherits-chain walk (WIProgression.granted_skills/_collect_inherited, data/classes.json): ice_mage `inherits` mage, so a held ice_mage:10 auto-grants BOTH its own level-10 kit (ice_shard, icy_floor) AND every mage grant evaluated at level 10 (frost_bolt/quick_cast/light from mage L1, flame_jet/mana_shield from mage L2) with zero hand-stuffed player_skills -- classes:{ice_mage:10} alone is sufficient (do not add icy_floor to player_skills; that would mask an inheritance regression instead of proving it). The resulting combat kit (weapon-gated but none of these carry a `weapon` tag, so all seven pass through unfiltered; only the four with contexts:combat + ap_cost>0 populate the hotbar) orders ice_shard, icy_floor, frost_bolt, flame_jet -> hotbar slots 3/4/5/6 (Attack=1, Dash=2). combat_autoplay never casts a spell for the pc (melee-profile default, see CLAUDE.md Gotchas), so ice_floor_loop drives the icy_floor cast by hand via a real hotbar press, same idiom as status_first_encounter's frost_bolt proof. rng_state '9' held on first try (icy_floor has NO hit roll anywhere in its path -- fully deterministic; the fight finish is combat_autoplay's basic melee attacks against inert 21-HP-class training dummies, the same low-risk shape status_first_encounter already established).
